From Florence, after a «painful» journey, she asks her to send two Sisters.

A.M.F. My daughter,

  1. My journey, as usual, was painful, for I had a bad headache,1 so that on reaching home I threw myself on the bed in despair.

  2. Listen, as soon as you receive this, send the two sisters, Sr. A. Martina and Sr. A. Stanislaa, here at once; the fare from Pisa to Florence is F. 12.70 for the two.2

  3. Tell Fr Accinelli to buy me one of the cheap chalices and give it to the sisters you are to send. Be as quick as you can; at once, at once.

  4. For your guidance, when I leave I shall let you know two days beforehand.3 I hope those from Piacenza have reached you.4

Goodbye, in haste, your [...]; greet Accinelli for me, and believe me yours

Affect. M. R.

1 As usual. The Mother bore travelling badly.

2 Sr. A. Martina Chigi and Sr. A. Stanislaa Vignoli. The fare for both from Pisa to Florence came to Fr. 12.70.

3 I shall let you know two days before I leave.

4 those: the sisters from Piacenza.

Willing to send the Sisters, she makes some remarks about their number and the service they are to give in the school and possibly in the hospital.

[Dear Mr Mayor,]

  1. I have received your esteemed letter of 27 April. Before sending you the papers Your Lordship requests,2 allow me to make some observations about the said Sisters, which Your Lordship in your wisdom will surely approve.

  2. Having to send three sisters there on a stipend of 1,100 Lire, and not knowing for certain what the Comune3 will give them, this is too little.

  3. Moreover, as I cannot clearly make out from your esteemed letter whether these three Sisters are also to look after the Hospital, this could not possibly be accepted, because the three who teach cannot have duties other than those of the school itself.4

  4. Though sending you 3 at your expense, I would add one more at my own expense, providing them with their bed.

  5. As for the hospital, Your Lordship should know that we have not only the management but also the care and nursing of the sick themselves, doing all the menial work and the cooking; and so in the Hospitals entrusted to us we have only one attendant, who gives the men those services modesty does not allow us; for the rest...

  6. As for teachers, from what I gather from yours, one qualified teacher with a trainee assistant would suffice. Kindly reply as soon as possible,5 as I need to know how to arrange things, having many other requests for other houses. Confident of a kind

reply, I sign myself with every esteem

Humble Servant Sr. A. Rosa Gattorno

1 The date is inferred from the Mayor's reply dated 1 May 1876.

2 Send the papers: prepare the documents requested: qualifications, birth certificates, etc.

3 the Comune: perhaps the Congregation of Charity that ran the hospital.

4 In his reply of 1 May the Mayor explains that two Sisters are enough to teach the girls, as only the first and second classes are involved; the third Sister «should for the present be concerned only with the general supervision of this small hospital and the care of the linen, since at present the hospital itself has two attendants, one for the men and the other for the women».

5 As soon as possible, also because the Mayor wanted the Sisters on the spot within ten days.

Intending to open an institution for the free education of deaf girls, she asks for suitable municipal premises to be made available.

[Most Illustrious Councillors,]

  1. I, the undersigned, placing my trust in the kindness that inspires Your Most Illustrious Lordships, turn to you to obtain a favour that will benefit this city and Province.

  2. It is my intention to open a home2 for Deaf-mute girls, who will be taken in, maintained and educated free of charge; but to carry out this wish I need to find suitable premises, as I have none available for the purpose.

  3. I applied for it to the Honourable Municipal Board,3 to whom I also explained my intention, and was told to turn to Your Most Illustrious Lordships; this I now do, earnestly begging you to grant me free municipal premises for a free home for Deaf-mute girls, leaving it to your wisdom as regards both the education and the healthiness of the place.

  4. The benefit this work will bring, and above all the philanthropy of Your Most Illustrious Lordships, make me hope to obtain what I ask,4 and in this hope I remain

Your Most Illustrious Lordships'

Most devoted Servant

Sr. A. Rosa Gattorno

1 The letter is undated. It is presumed to belong to this period on the basis of some direct historical evidence: the Cardinal Protector Giuseppe Berardi wrote to M. Rosa on 21.4.1876: «...I am glad to learn that you are opening new houses, among them another in Piacenza itself». AFSA BGpl-1876. Moreover, the Mother was having two Sisters trained at an institute of Religious in Como: Sr. A. Colomba Rimassa and Sr. A. Benigna Mazzini. The former wrote to her on 10.4.76: «...the Director, Fr Serafino... encouraged us in this study so as to give the Bishop the consolation of soon seeing a house for deaf-mutes opened in Piacenza». AFSA D5.

2 Home (ricovero): the name then given to welfare and training institutions.

3 This letter has not been preserved.

4 The reply and other documents on the matter are still missing from the AFSA.

She will send her the «dialogue» as soon as possible. She encourages her to keep up her school work and explains how to manage in the summer.

A.M.F.

My daughter,

  1. I received your little letter and hear what you say about the dialogue; I wrote at once to Onorata to write it and send it to me; as soon as I have it [...].1

  2. Take care of yourself; I hear what a celebration you had in Via Pettinari.2 See, Daughter, how sweet the Lord is! Surely He wants to be loved and served as He deserves.

  3. As for that wretched woman, don't worry, for the Lord knows well how to uncover things; unfortunately He will make her known and she will be put to shame;3 all too soon we see our misdeeds come to light; so courage!

  4. Listen, so as not to have to write again, for I have too much to do, I tell you now what I would like you to do when you have held the June examinations. At the end, as it will be very hot then and it is not wise to keep school, for otherwise you certainly will not hold out,4 it is better to do this: all those at the Fornaci will come to the Parrocchietta and you will go to Rome; then when the others come to Piacenza, if you are not well you will come too.5

  5. And Sr. A. Crocifissa can manage with the others; they can keep the girls occupied and meanwhile teach a little Christian doctrine.6 Do you think I am right? I believe so. Goodbye; I am your Affect. M., who wishes you a thousand blessings, and am

your affect. M. R.

1 She needed the «dialogue» for the end-of-year performance. M. Rosa will have the teacher Onorata Colli write it and will send it as soon as she receives it.

2 On Sunday 30 April Cardinal Giuseppe Berardi had gathered the Sisters of the Rome Communities in Via Pettinari, and they had dined and rejoiced together.

3 It is not known to whom she alludes, as the Sister's letter is missing. Wretched... put to shame: poor thing... will be humiliated.

4 She was in delicate health.

5 She is to proceed thus: all the Sisters of the Via Fornaci school move to the Parrocchietta, you go to Rome, and so you can join the Sisters coming to Piacenza for their vows.

6 Sr. A. Crocifissa Fiocchi and the other Sisters of the Parrocchietta can keep the girls occupied and teach them the catechism.

She sets out the essential conditions for sending the Sisters.

Dear Mr Mayor,

  1. In reply to your esteemed letter of 8 May,1 the agreement is settled for 3 Sisters at 1,700 Lire a year, in addition to everything in the first request.2

  2. For the moment I send you the name of the Qualified Teacher, and that of the Assistant, as I do not have the diploma and other papers here in this house where I am passing through;3 but I shall write at once to have them sent to me, and as soon as I have them I shall forward them to Your Lordship.

Please accept my sentiments of deep esteem

Humble Servant Sr. A. Rosa Gattorno

Travel paid and only one Diploma.

1 The correspondence had continued, cf. L 188. The Mother's L of 4 May is missing, but the Mayor's of 8 May has been preserved; he restricts the agreement to teaching only, setting aside the hospital service.

2 Cf. L 188,2.

3 Cf. ibid., n. 2.

She advises sending an ailing Sister to Sestri for a change of air. She will go to Ferrara and then return to Piacenza.

A.M.F. My daughter,

  1. I have just received yours telling me that the newly-weds have arrived in Genoa;1 I wrote to them, addressing the letter to Mamma, that is, to the house in Scurreria.2 So you are truly everyone's refuge; surely they will have been glad to stay, being free to do as they thought best. A pity you are so cramped; if you could see how big it is here! You surely ought not to be so badly off.3

  2. Listen, that sister who was in such poor shape, you know, the one you told me was from Cortemaggiore and whose periods were irregular; I think you might send her to Sestri for a while to see whether she recovers.4 What do you say? Otherwise she will need a change of air while there is still time; write and tell me.5

  3. Listen, I had thought of leaving for Ferrara on Saturday,6 but address your letters to Piacenza, where I am giving orders for them all to be kept for me. And try to go to the blind girls again to see whether the little machines [are] there; otherwise I fear they will forget the little they know.7 Goodbye, dear Daughter; please have them pray, for I am in extreme need. Goodbye, your

Most affect. M. R.

1 The newly-weds: Carlotta and Gaspare Barbiellini. Cf. L 183,8.

2 in Scurreria: in Via Scurreria.

3 You are so cramped: the house was inadequate for the number of Sisters (almost

thirty). Big here = space, cf. L 183,6. Surely you ought not to be so

badly housed for lack of room. They had not yet managed to find

a larger house. Cf. L 24,2; 47,1.

4 That Sister who is unwell, you could send her to Sestri, where the air

is good.

5 Let me know what you have done.

6 Saturday, 13 May.

7 Evidently some blind girls had been taken in at the Sampierdarena

Institute. The superior was to see about obtaining the "little machines"

so that they could practise writing, and so avoid forgetting

what they had learned.

She arranges the transfer of some Sisters. She asks her to buy and send twelve beds. A Sister will arrive from Piacenza bringing the ducks.

A.M.F.

My daughter,

1. Listen, if the sister recovers, keep her, as you say, the one from Cortemaggiore.1 On my orders you will go and fetch Sr. A. Graziosa, Sr. A. Chiara and Sr. A. Federica from the S. P. D'Arena hospital; you will take there the two I sent you last, who were still here, that is, the ones sent, whom I had brought from Piacenza.2 Do you understand? See that you do at once what I tell you.

2. Now I would ask you another big favour: to have twelve iron beds sent to me like yours, with the curtains, that is, the rods for hanging curtains; in short, like the ones you have. Listen, I shall pay you for them little by little; take your time, a year or at least six months; what do you say? But I would like them soon, as soon as possible.3

3. For the rest, I hear that all is going well, and I bless God for it; I shall send you a Sister whom you will send on to the hospital. She will bring you some ducks: 12 are for Mamma,4 and you will take them to her at once; the others are for you. Take them to Mamma at once.

4. So you need no permission to go and see her, because whenever she wishes you may go, and with whomever she wishes. Goodbye, your; tell Fr Accinelli to write to me at once whether he has received my letter dated today. Many greetings to the sisters, and believe me your affect.

M. R.

1 Cf. L ..

2 Sr. A. Graziosa Danieli, Sr. A. Chiara Rossi, Sr. A. Federica Anfossi; cf.

L 194,1; 195,1. You will accompany the two who last arrived there from Piacenza. Cf. L 187,

n. 4. '

3 I would like them as soon as possible.

4 This is Signora Adelaide, M. Rosa's mother.

192,2.

She arranges for a Sister to leave for Ovada and orders her not to send her any food.

A.M.F. My daughter,

1. A line to tell you to send Sr. A. Graziosa to Ovada;1 of course it would be better if Fr Antonio could accompany her.2 Meanwhile I am writing to the President; or else, as she has to take the baths, I think she could stay a while in the S. Pier d'Arena house, and so take the baths.3

2. I am sending you the ducklings: 4 for you and 12 for Mamma. Take them to her at once or they will suffer; feed them first.4

3. I forbid you by virtue of holy obedience to send me fish, do you understand? I have orange-flower water to spare. For charity's sake, don't waste money.5

4. Another obedience: I absolutely do not want you to go to the sick. I am sending you this Sr. A. Celeste, who is very dear. For charity's sake, take care of yourself

Goodbye, your Affect. M. R.

1 Sr. A. Graziosa Danieli was being transferred to the hospital community at

Ovada. Cf. L 193,1.

2 It would be better if Fr Antonio Accinelli could accompany her.

3 As she had to take a course of baths, it would be better for her to go first to

Sampierdarena.

4 She is sending the ducklings. Cf. L 192,3.

5 Cf. L 112,1.

She is to take two Sisters to the hospital and hurry the delivery of the beds.

A.M.F.

My daughter,

1. You will take Sr. A. Chiara and the one I sent you last, Sr. A. Celeste, to the hospital, and you will take Sr. A. Annunciata,1 at once, as soon as you receive this.

2. I hear they are giving you the beds; now I would like you to tell them I want them for 5 or at the latest 6 June, and earlier if possible.2 Dear daughter, I have a visitation here, and you can imagine how worried I am. I know it is not liked that I leave the beds like this without curtains.3 Try to get them to me.

Goodbye. I am in a hurry, your

Affect. M.

1 Sr. A. Chiara Rossi, Sr. A. Celeste Socci, Sr. A. Annunciata Aliverti.

2 Cf. L 193,2.

3 The curtains round the bed served to screen it off like a cubicle.

She expresses gratitude for his calling the FSA to his Diocese. She accepts his proposal and asks how to arrange the sending of the Sisters.

Most Reverend Excellency,

1. The Reverend Missionary Fr Enrico Tipoli has informed me that Your Most Rev. Excellency wishes to have the poor Daughters of Saint Anne in your City;1 and while thanking you for this kindness towards us, I praise God for inspiring it and accept your proposal, assuring you that we shall do our best to make our feeble work beneficial to your Diocesans.

2. We accept the terms2 Your Most Rev. Excellency offers us, trusting in Divine providence, which will not abandon these poor servants of His, who, blessed by Your Excellency, hope to prove worthy of the kindness you show them.

3. I beg you to tell me by letter how I should arrange to send the sisters there, among whom will be the qualified Teacher you desire.3

4. I hope all will go well, and from this we shall conclude that it is the Lord's will for the poor Daughters of Saint Anne to go there and give their very humble service.

5. Meanwhile we are offering special prayers that the Lord may show us His divine will ever more clearly and enable us to be useful to Your Most Rev. Excellency and act according to your wishes.

6. Your Excellency, send us your pastoral blessing, which will protect us on our journey, with a line to tell me how we should arrange to come, and meanwhile I am sure we shall have our travelling expenses paid.4

Bless the least of all, who remains humbly at your feet

Your most devoted Servant Sister ANNA ROSA GATTORNO

1 Through Fr Enrico Tipoli of the Priests of the Mission she had learned of his wish

to have the FSA at Tropea (CZ).

2 We accept the terms: a rent-free furnished house, an annual payment of L.

600 for two Sisters. Cf. L Mgr. Vaccari AFSA, CvIM.60.

3 For the Bishop's reply cf. L 202.

4 Paid: defrayed.

She gladly takes the opportunity to have her letter delivered to him. She is close to him and interested in his business; she has sent him the linen. She encourages him, urging him to look after his health. Carlotta and Gaspare are at Albaro.

My son,

1. Onorata tells me there is a safe opportunity to send you letters, and I take it at once. Yes, my dear Alessandro, believe that this poor Mother of yours would like an opportunity to write to you every day.

2. I have given the Fr. 40 to the person you told me; just think how I long to hear that you are settled at last, and I am deeply grieved because you are always up in the air, and what is more you are no longer with your cousin.2 Patience!

3. I hope you have received the linen, and the things your uncles sent you to sell, goods and wine. I also saw a magnificent watch.3

4. You see that we all think of you, and it is not true, as you say, that we forget you. No, no! Oh! my God! If you could see how many prayers this poor mother of yours offers, you surely could not entertain the troubling thought that I do not think of you. Oh! My dear Son! One day you will see whether I have thought of you.

5. You ask me about the furniture; your uncles tell me it is not worth it because it costs too much; I sent you the linen at once. I hope you will be able to do something with the goods your uncles sent you.

6. Do not lose heart if something should happen to you on account of your cousin, for you will see that money comes and goes, but the rest, that is health, cannot be recovered. So take care of yourself and remember that everything on this earth comes to an end and only good

and evil remain to us, and these two alone we take with us into eternity; good will win us eternal life, and evil, alas! I cannot even think of it, for it would be a grief that would kill me.4 Shall I never see my dear Son again for all eternity? No, Our Lady will keep him good for me and I shall enjoy him for ever.

7. Your sister is still at Albaro with her husband; I assure you that you have gained a true brother, and when you see him you will be pleased.

8. I assure you I have been left in debt on all sides, but with a little economy I hope to recover and be able to satisfy you too by sending you what you ask; but for now you will surely understand.5 Won't you? So be patient, and I hope you will be pleased with what I have done.

Goodbye, dear son; the Father,6 who is here, sends his greetings, and I embrace you, remaining your

affect. M. ROSA GATTORNO

1 The date is inferred from the contents and especially from what is said about

Carlotta and Gaspare. Married on 26 April, they had left for Lourdes, had returned

to Genoa on 8 May (cf. L 192,1) and then stayed at Albaro.

2 Alessandro's letter to which the Mother refers is dated 18.4.1876. He

speaks at length about his cousin Emanuele, his bankruptcy and why he is no longer

with him.

3 His uncles Federico and Francesco Gattorno had helped him a great deal, as

the Mother says here. Cf. AFSA. GF1M.

4 Her grief is sharpened by what Alessandro wrote about his cousin: he "is

a freemason".

5 In two letters he had asked her for financial help of 3,000 to 5,000 francs.

6 Father Tornatore.

She sends her two letters to deliver in person.

A.M.F.

My daughter,

1. You will receive these two letters;1 take one to Advocate Boccardo, you know, Sr. A. Vincenza's uncle, the one who is to handle the Ricchino lawsuit, and the other is for that judge Arrighetti whom you went to see with Sr. A. Benedetta; Fr Accinelli can show you where they live. Take Boccardo the life of Sr. A. Vincenza2 together with the letter, at once, at once. I think I have made myself clear.

Goodbye, courage, and much more in person

your most affect. M.R.

1 The two letters have not been preserved.

2 The biography compiled by Onorata Colli and published in Piacenza by

Tip. Favari e Breda in 1875. Cf. L 80,3.

She arranges the transfer of two Sisters. She has not yet received everything she asked her to buy.

A.M.F.

My daughter,

1. I hear you have sent Sr. A. Antonina to the new house.1 Listen, for pity's sake, take her out at once and put in Sr. A. ..., the one who had erysipelas, as the air will do her good; and tell her for charity's sake to be good, do the cooking and try to be exemplary; not to behave like a girl, but always be serious and composed, at home and out of doors.

2. Yesterday I sent you a packet with letters inside and also a life of Sr. A. Vincenza to take to her uncle, Advocate Boccardo.2

3. I hope you have understood: this Sister, Sr. A. Antonina,3 you may send to Sestri for a while to take some baths; meanwhile I also enclose a line for the Superior.

Goodbye, your

Affect. M.

4. I have just received the tartan [cloth], but not the pasta; I hope it

will arrive.

1 The new house. Cf. L 204, n. 2.

2 Cf. L 198.

3 Sr. A. Antonina Gabiotti.

Most Holy Father,

1. As Your Holiness has deigned to grant our poor Institute His Eminence Cardinal Berardi as Protector,1 I make bold to beg Your Holiness that His Eminence may come here to visit the Mother House,2 so that he may see better and become thoroughly imbued with our spirit; and also, for matters of no small importance to the Work, I should like to submit everything to his most wise counsel.

The petitioner, confident of the favour, having kissed the Sacred Foot, prostrates herself with her forehead to the ground

Your Holiness's

Lowliest daughter

Sister A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 Card. Giuseppe Berardi had succeeded Cardinal Luigi Vannicelli. Cf.

L 183, n. 3.

2 Beg. Because of his high offices (judge of the Apostolic Camera, mem-

ber of the S. Congregation of Bishops and Regulars, etc.) the Cardinal could not

leave Rome at will. Indeed, to M. Rosa's invitation to come to Piacenza

he had replied that he "depended entirely on the will of the Holy Father" and that

therefore "a request from someone else" was needed. (L to M.R. 21.4.76). On 13

June he told her he would come to Piacenza for the feast of Saint Anne. Cf. AFSA GBpl.
She asks for permission for Cardinal Berardi to come to the Mother House in Piacenza.

Summons to Piacenza, the Mother House, for the Spiritual Exercises.

A.M.F.

Superior,

1. Having decided that all the Superiors are to make the Holy Exercises at the Mother House in Piacenza, I am giving you too timely notice to arrange your House so that everything runs in order during your absence.1

2. Bring with you the half-yearly accounts for 1876, from 1 January to the end of June.

3. Let me know by letter how many religious with you have completed two and three years of vocation.2

4. The purpose of this Circular is for you to be at this Mother House by the 16th of next month.

Sr. A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 That is, assign to one Sister the task of replacing her in running the

House and give each Sister her duties precisely and clearly.

2 This was to determine the names of the Sisters who would take their vows on the

feast of Saint Anne that year.

She has received his letter and replies that she cannot send only two Sisters, but three. She awaits his word for their departure.

Most Reverend Excellency,

1. I have just finished reading your most venerated letter.1 God grant that, according to His will, we may give satisfaction to Your Most Rev. Excellency, who so kindly deigns to welcome us into your Diocese; and I pray most fervently to the Lord that all may turn out for the greater good of souls and the sanctification of those to whom this Mission is given.

2. Your Most Rev. Excellency speaks of only two Sisters,2 and this must surely be because I did not explain myself well enough in the letter I sent you. Two Sisters alone cannot form a community; for Your Excellency's sake I can agree to send just Three, with the [hope] of increasing them later.

3. Your Excellency asks me the name of the Qualified Teacher who will come. She is Sr. A. Adelaide Cervini, qualified for 10 years.

4. As for the Rules, we shall bring them when the sisters come, and when Your Most Rev. Excellency has read them, kindly return them. Meanwhile I send you the purpose of our Institution.3

5. As regards our coming, it will take place when Your Most Rev. Excellency thinks fit and lets me know, and I shall be delighted to send you the sisters.4

Deign to grant your Pastoral blessing to the least Servant of the Lord

Sr. A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 The L is dated 30 May 1876 (AFSA CvIM).

2 He speaks quite clearly of two Sisters for the school.

3 Evidently she enclosed a separate summary.

4 The Bishop had specified on this point: "the coming of the Sisters, though most

eagerly desired, could not take place before next October".

Her daughter, a Novice in the Institute, wants to go home. She sends her back, explaining the reasons for her return.

[Dear Madam,]

1. As you will see from your daughter's letter, she absolutely refuses to remain in our Institute any longer, so I must remove her habit and let her return home.

2. Please note that in the two years2 we have had her with us she has always been ill and was no small burden to us, for her illness required much care from doctors, many medicines and very nourishing food; the doctors who treated her can testify [to] this, as can the Paper she herself leaves with us, truthfully attesting what she has received from our poor Institute.

3. Now that she is completely cured she drives us to despair by insisting on leaving and going home, threatening to make a scene if we prevent it. So I am obliged to let her leave for home next Monday.3 Her conduct has always been reprehensible,4 but always excused because of her illness. I believe this is enough without saying more, and I sign myself

Humble Servant Sr. A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 She was the mother of the Novice Sr. A. Marta Fioraghi, of Ferrara. Her name was

taken from the Register of Postulants.

2 The young woman had entered the Institute on 10 April 1874.

3 She drives us to despair, in that she insists arrogantly. She will leave

next Monday, 12 June.

4 Reprehensible: blameworthy.

She invites her to Piacenza for the Superiors' Spiritual Exercises. Directions on founding a new work in Genoa.

A.M.F.

Superior,

1. Having decided that all the Superiors are to make the Holy Exercises at the Mother House in Piacenza,1 I am giving you too timely notice to arrange your House so that all runs in order during your absence.

2. Bring with you the half-yearly accounts for 1876, from 1 January to the end of June.

3. Let me know by letter how many Religious with you have completed two and three years of vocation. These exercises will begin on 16 July.

4. You ask me whom you should appoint as Superior at S. Antonino.2 Sr. A. Elisa provisionally; tell her that after Saint Anne's I shall send her the permanent Superior, as the exercises are on the 16th of that month and it would not be worth her making the journey for so few days.3 You tell me we are to provide the linen; I say no, for I agreed that he must provide everything. Be careful, dear daughter, for otherwise they are all the same, they want to profit at our expense.4

5. The beds have arrived safely and are already set up, as are the chairs, the tartan [cloth] and the lamps.5 Carlotta will not be back for another 5 days; they are both well.

6. As for the other two Sisters, you could take one from Sestri, Sr. A. ..., I don't remember her name, one of the little ones who go begging, a plump one, I think it is Sr. A. Marcellina. If you can manage without them and send them some of your own in Genoa, that will be better,6 all the

more so as now, with summer coming, you will not have so many sick. Do as you think best, your

Most affect. M. R. GATTORNO

1 Cf. L201.

2 At S. Antonino. At the Parish of S. Antonino the FSA were entrusted with

a parish elementary school.

3 You will send Sr. A. Elisa Corsini provisionally. After Saint Anne's the Superior

would go. It was not worth her going earlier for only a few days,

as she had to be in Piacenza from 16 to 26 July for the Spiritual Exercises.

4 The linen for the new house was to be supplied by the parish priest; he must pro-

vide everything. Be careful, for they are all the same, they want to speculate (profit)

to our disadvantage.

5 All the material ordered and sent by her has arrived. The lamps (the two

candelabra) for Carlotta are fine. Cf. L 193,2.

6 If you can manage without them, if you can avoid moving Sisters from other houses

and send some from your own community, that will be better.

She complains of her disobedience in continuing to send fish. She sends some ducks by two Sisters, whom she is to place in the community.

A.M.F. My daughter,

1. First of all I must complain, because you have not obeyed me by stopping sending fish and certain trifles; now I tell you that I shall send back the first lot I receive, you may be sure of it, except the pasta, which we have already agreed on.1

2. If a few more copies of the Settimana Religiosa2 could be had, you would do me a great favour, as I badly need them; I have received the books, thank you. As for the Sisters you are to send, I told you: for now Sr. A. Elisa,3 and I shall send one from here, who will hand you this letter and will have some ducks for the M.sa Edvige, Sr. A. Benedetta's sister-in-law. Take them to her at once.

3. I am sending you two sisters; one is for S. P. D'Arena: Sr. A. Atanasia will be for S. P. D'Arena and Sr. A. Ampeglia for S. Antonino.4 The latter is well educated, as is the one going to S. P. d'Arena; for the third you will send Sr. A. Faustina, who can do a little cooking and meanwhile rest a bit; I hope she will have come back from the nuns and they will no longer need her.5 If she should still go to them, we shall put in someone else.

She stresses some aspects of the contract, pointing out the obligations undertaken towards the municipal Administration and her right to transfer and replace the Sisters.

[Dear Mr Mayor,]

1. In reply to your esteemed note of the 3rd inst., I take the liberty of observing that, from the moment you saw fit to entrust the running of your girls' schools and hospital to a Religious Institute, there was no longer any question of invoking the privileges arising from the two articles you cite, whether in favour of the individual teachers or of the Comune.1

2. Yes, I readily understand that a private contract made with an individual is quite a different thing.2

3. The Contract was made with me as Superior General. The individuals working there are my representatives in fulfilling obligations undertaken not by them but by me. In binding myself as Superior to run your schools and hospital, I undertook to keep there persons with the required qualifications, without however binding myself to particular individuals or particular periods as regards their stay, and this for compelling reasons of this Institute.

4. This being so, article 77 invoked in favour of your Comune seems to me out of place. At most I might accept it as valid3 if, regarding what I contracted with you, I wished without reasonable cause to withdraw from the commitment undertaken for your schools and abandon the house without notice; but to claim that I, on whom alone the responsibility towards you rests, may not replace the present teachers with others equally capable, as the Institute requires,4 is to tell me that you are tired of the Daughters of Saint Anne, and to

force me without more ado to recall them and withdraw them from that house, so that you may avail yourselves of those who know how and are able to serve you better.

5. Such is the conclusion your stated demands lead me to. And here I end, reserving for another time, if need be, my reply to the second point, concerning the diploma for the infant school, but asking Your Lordship for a line in reply informing me of the decisions your Comune will take following this letter.5

And with due consideration and esteem I remain

Your Lordship's

Humble Servant

Sr. A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 The articles she refers to read: "Art. 74. A teacher whose

election and confirmation have been approved shall remain in office for the whole period stated in the

appointment; where the period is neither stated nor limited, the election shall be deemed

to be for three years". "Art. 77. These provisions concern both the Comuni

and the teachers".

2 The Mother rightly points out the difference between a personal contract and

one made with an Institute.

3 I might consider it valid (good).

4 The Mother never gave up the freedom to change the Sisters according to the needs

of the Institute.

5 The reply was not long in coming. On 16 July the Mayor restated his prin-

ciples: "The Municipality of Mercatello, in the contract made with the local Congregation

of Charity regarding the service of the schools up to the fourth elementary class, has

agreed to accept the Sisters of Saint Anne, three in number, qualified and personally

subject to the provisions of the law both as to appointment and dis-

missal". Later, however, an understanding was reached about changing the

teachers, by means of appointment for one school year. Cf. L 226.

The Holy Father Pius IX has raised the feast of Saint Anne to a "double of the first class with octave". Sisters making their vows for the first time or renewing them are to apply. The Superiors are to send the names of the Sisters of their communities and of those studying for the teaching qualification.

A.M.F.

My dearest daughters in J. C.,

1. The feast of our Holy Mother, glorious Saint Anne, is approaching. This year her feast has a special feature distinguishing it from previous years: His Holiness Pope Pius IX, gloriously reigning, has raised it for our Institute to a feast of obligation and a Double of the first class with octave.

2. Therefore on the Holy Mother's day we are strictly bound to hear Holy Mass and abstain from all servile work; that is, on that day it is not lawful to work.

3. This is a most distinguished glory with which the Holy Father has honoured our Institute, with the honour given to the greatest Saints of the Church.

4. It is also a new testimony that the Holy Father has honoured our Institute by counting it among the Institutes recognised by the Church.1 We therefore advise the Superiors that on that day they inform the Priests who come to celebrate Holy Mass in our Chapels that for us it is a feast of the first class with octave, so that they know what ceremonies to use.2

5. We also recall that on the feast of the Holy Mother

those completing three years of novitiate make their Holy Vows for the first time, and those who have already made them renew them.3 So the former must ask us in good time for leave to make them, and the latter for leave to renew them. On this occasion we also ask the Superiors to send us the first name and surname of every sister in their communities and also the personal number, that is, of the things they have for their use.

6. Likewise let them send us the names of the sisters we entrusted to them to study under the respective teachers in our schools, so as to qualify them to sit the examination this year, and have them ready for when we order them to come here to the Mother House.

7. We trust you will pay serious attention to all the points we have mentioned and carry them all out promptly.

Fr G. B. TORNATORE

M. A. ROSA GATTORNO

8. P.S. Send the timetable our boarders follow and the

prayers they say to the Holy Mother.

2 So that they keep to the prescribed rubrics.

3 First profession was made after three years of Novitiate. For the feast

of Saint Anne 1876 there were many professions. Cf. AFSA - Register of Professions

She has summoned her, but she has obstinately refused to come. So she writes to her denouncing her serious administrative irregularities in the hospital. She begs her to stop and entrusts her to God for healing.

A.M.F. My daughter,

1. As soon as I can hold the pen I address these two lines to you, which I do not know whether you will understand aright. Listen, since you obstinately refuse to come, I am obliged to write to you by registered letter;2 this worries me immensely and the very thought of it tears my heart.

2. Ah! if only you had come! We would have talked calmly in person, without agitation, and reasoned as Mother and daughter about what to do. Patience! my sins allow it to be so. In all things may the most holy will of my God be done.

3. Let us place ourselves in the presence of our Crucified Lord, and listen to me with resignation, for I have no wish at all to be either cruel or unjust.3

4. Well then, I have been told by a trustworthy person that you have an ounce or two taken from the portion of meat that goes to the sick and keep it for the community, and the same with the soup. Alas, blessed daughter, this is a sin, an offence against God! To defraud the poor sick!!...

5. Alas! They said they are certain about the meat, we know it, and that if the cooks were called they would have to swear to the truth. They are victims, because they are under strict orders. Daughter, stop for pity's sake, if this is true, though to calm my agitation I

push it away and keep telling myself: it is not true, it cannot be true.

6. That is why I wanted you. Oh, you have caused me extreme sorrow and mortal anguish; the state of my health is pitiful; but it is little enough, if only it suffices to bring you back to yourself and into the arms of your God.

7. Oh! how painful it was to see all the Superiors come into my arms and only one missing; and not even the second or third time did she heed me!4 It is for You, my God, to heal this creature.

(Her) your most affect. MOTHER ROSA GATTORNO

3 In the presence of our Crucified Lord: under His gaze she wants to "speak the

Chiede la rescissione della Convenzione ed esprime le gravi ragioni che la inducono a questa decisione.

Ill.mo Signor Presidente,

1. Si è con mio sommo rincrescimento che mi trovo obbligata di inviarle la presente, la quale ha per principale scopo di dichiararle che intendo sia sciolto ogni convenzione fra la mia Istituzione e l'amministrazione dell'Ospedale fatta il [6.6.1876] e ciò basato sui fatti, che non permetterebbero di oltre proseguire senza pregiudizio della giustizia, dell'umanità e della morale.

2. Io partii da Piacenza, quantunque indisposta, onde venire all'ospedale per verificare voci che mi giunsero colà, voci che accennavano a poco buon trattamento degli ammalati e non meno buona condotta della Superiora, che io aveva messo a capo delle infermiere.1 Con mia grande sorpresa mi trovai di fronte una schiera di nemici che d'accordo mi barravano il passo per impedire forse ch'io scoprissi la verità, la qual cosa non poteva altro che convincermi essere purtroppo vere le voci, alle quali avrei ben desiderato dare una smentita.

3. La S. V. Ill.ma non fu meno aspra nel ricevermi e, pregatola d'altro abboccamento, mi fu concesso gentilmente pel giorno appresso; io non potei intervenire causa la mia malferma salute e rimandatolo mi si fece sperare pel giovedì venturo. La Direzione non volle essere meno contraria e si compiaceva pur essa d'intralciare il mio lavoro di verifica. I giorni scorsi poi mandai suore mie per parlare colle Suore dell'ospedale e vennero scacciate senza che potessero parlare con persona alcuna; le suore poi dell'ospedale vennero impedite di comunicare con me. Quale interpetrazione dovrei dare ad una simile condotta?

4. Io dirò francamente: abuso di convenienza2 fra Amministrazione, Direzione e Superiora. In quanto poi all'avere impedito alle Suore del mio Istituto di parlare con altre dell'ospedale è tutto una buona baroncinata medioevale3 di che solo la giustìzia potrebbe impegnarsene; e per mio conto intanto mi è debito farle conoscere che le Suore del mio Istituto non hanno nessun vincolo fuori quello che le lega all'impegno che si prendono verso l'umanità di assisterla, curarla, alleviarla, e perciò la pressione, l'ordinazione che loro si volle dare di non comunicare colle altre è atto arbitrario da non trovare il termine per poterlo classificare e pel quale protesto altamente in nome della giustizia.

5. Mi è duopo cessare non volendo finire in una pleiade d'accusa in forma requisitoria e solo un'ultima parola per raccomandar caldamente a cotest'Amministrazione di voler prendere in considerazione questa pratica al più presto possibile per risparmiare maggior male e poter definire il tutto nel modo più conciliante ancora possibile.4

6. Faccio altresì calda preghiera onde si voglia far cessare quel

l'impedimento di comunicazione fra le suore dell'ospedale e quelle

di altre mie case di beneficenza.5

7. In quanto poi al modo e al tempo, in cui le mie suore dovranno abbandonare l'ospedale si combinerà d'accordo, non volendo io certo portare il minimo danno all'andamento dell'amministrazione interna che poi sarebbe a danno del povero ammalato; ma confido sarà provvisto al più presto e così potrò ritirare le suore tutte.

8. Nella speranza di vedere accolta questa mia domanda in considerazione di tutte le disgraziate6 considerazioni mi pregio di dichiararmi sua

Dev.ma Serva Sr. A. ROSA GATTORNO

1 Cf. L 216, 4-5.

2 Abuso di convenienza = connivenza.

3 baroncinata medioevale, sopruso da Medioevo.

4 Nel modo più conciliante, più conveniente e di comune accordo.

5 Le Suore della Comunità di Sampierdarena e Genova.

6 disgraziate considerazioni: spiacevoli.

[Carissime figliole,]

1. Ecco, Figliuole dilettissime, che per la misericordia di Dio siamo entrate nel nuovo anno. Due affetti ci si devono risvegliare nei nostri cuori; l'uno di riconoscenza, e l'altro di dolore; di riconoscenza verso il nostro Padre celeste per le numerose benedizioni che in tutto il corso dell'anno adesso finito ha versate sovra il nostro Istituto; una grazia assai rimarchevole, e che merita di essere menzionata la prima, si è quella d'averci dato un nuovo Protettore nella Persona dell'Eminentissimo Cardinale Giuseppe Berardi, questo Cardinale dal momento che prese la protezione del nostro Istituto, che fu appunto nei principi dell'anno 1876, si mostrò Padre veramente amante.1

2. Egli non cessò mai di dare attestati di amore paterno: un attestato assai sensibile di questo suo amore, fu la visita che si compiacque fare alla nostra casa Madre, questa visita ce la fece col consenso di Sua Santità2 e vi celebrò la festa della Santa Madre. La presenza del Porporato accrebbe assai la solennità di quella festa poiché

vi attirò a venerare la Santa Madre una moltitudine grande di distinti personaggi. Questa visita fu un vero trionfo per il nostro povero Istituto. Aprì gli occhi di molti che non lo curavano, molti che fin allora lo sprezzavano cambiarono il dispregio in istima, sicché questa visita fu una insigne grazia che ci fece il Signore di averci dato un tanto Protettore; e dobbiamo pregarlo che ce lo conservi; e sempre più lo arricchisca di lumi e di forza per il bene del nostro Istituto.

3. Che diremo poi della grazia che ci ha fatto il Signore di continuare all'Istituto la speciale benevolenza del suo Vicario il Santo Padre Pio IX? Egli mostrò questa sua speciale bontà per l'Istituto ammettendoci più volte alla sua udienza;3 trattandoci con cordialità da Padre domandandoci con interessamento del progresso dell'Istituto.

4. Egli nutre un affetto singolare per il nostro Istituto, perché il nostro Istituto, fu suscitato dal Signore nella sua Chiesa, acciocché onori in modo speciale quella veneranda Matrona nel seno della quale è stato operato il mistero dell'Immacolato concepimento di Maria dalla definizione del quale mistero il Santo Padre pio IX ritrae quella gloria così grande,4 per la quale Egli risplende sovra tutti i Papi, come il sole risplende più delle stelle.

5. Ecco perché il nostro Istituto in questi suoi primordi il numero più grande di case le ha fondate e le va fondando nello stato del Papa,5 e dirò così attorno al suo Trono perché tra il S.to Padre Papa Pio IX, ed il nostro Istituto vi è una secreta simpatia, ed Egli a guisa di calamita se lo tira a sé e vuole che invada tutto il suo stato, prima di dilatarsi neEe altre parti del mondo, ma si sa che dove si porta l'affetto del Papa, ivi si porta l'affetto dei Vescovi e dei buoni fedeli.

6. Quindi è che i nostri Signori Vescovi ovunque siamo ci amano, e ci vedono volentieri così è dei fedeli: essi gradiscono le nostre funzioni, e moltissimi sono gli infermi di ogni condizione, che chiedono la nostra assistenza, tanto a domicilio che agli ospedali.

7. Intanto che in un ospedale dal quale la malizia dei tristi dovemmo nostro malgrado abbandonare quel sito, benché fossero immense le industrie che tennero per farci fermare di cui sempre abbiamo istanza e perché ci ritorniamo gli infermi piangono di non aver più le nostre cure, e alle loro lacrime si aggiungono anche quelle dei buoni di quella Città.6

8. Le nostre scuole poi sono numerosissime,7 e il Signore per intercessione della Santa Madre le benedice, e le giovanette vi progrediscono, e nelle virtù e nelle lettere. In quest'anno nuovo poi che

abbiamo messo che in tutte esse vi si onori il gaudio che la Santa Madre provò nell'Immacolato concepimento di Maria con tre Pater, Ave, Gloria i quali Pater sono come la divisa, che distingue le nostre scuole da quelle degli altri Istituti, le benedizioni vi saranno più abbondanti.

9. Una testimonianza dell'affetto che ci hanno i Vescovi ed i

popoli, l'abbiamo avuto nell'anno finito; in esso l'Istituto si è dilatato

e in fondazioni ed in personale, in una maniera prodigiosa, di

Case ne abbiamo fondate nove8 e di sorelle ne abbiamo vestite 76 e

morte 4.

10. Ecco come sono forti e numerosi i motivi che abbiamo, Figliuole dilettissime, di benedire e ringraziare il Signore. Ma abbiamo corrisposto a tante grazie? In generale, per grazia di Dio, le Sorelle corrispondono al fine della vocazione: il quale fine si è di imitare la Santa Madre osservando le Regole e di onorarne le prerogative; massime quella di essere Madre dell'Immacolata, onore che da noi le viene fatto, recitando nell'ore stabilite la giaculatoria dell'Istituto cioè: sia benedetta la gloriosa nostra Madre Sant'anna Madre dell'Immacolata,9 e recitandola con fervore, perché in questa giaculatoria vi si contiene una professione di fede colla quale noi crediamo che Maria nel seno della nostra Santa Madre, nel primo istante di sua concezione vi fu concepita immacolata, ossia senza macchia originale. E poiché questa giaculatoria è quasi continua dalla mattina alla sera così con essa l'Istituto fa come di continuo l'atto di fede dell'Immacolato concepimento di Maria.

11. Questa imitazione della Santa Madre e questa venerazione dei di Lei pregi è quell'opera che Iddio vuole da noi in quanto siamo Figlie di Sant'Anna, come testimonianza che l'amiamo. E perciò può dirsi che le Sorelle in generale amano di cuore il Signore, ma non di tutte è vero che nell'anno finito sono state fedeli all'imitare e venerare la Santa Madre, nel modo spiegato.

12. Faremo menzione di alcuni difetti nei quali difetti sono cadute; uno di questi difetti osservato anche dagli estranei, fu del poco buon comportamento quando vanno per istrada. Il portamento delle Figlie di Sant'Anna per istrada deve essere insieme disinvolto e modesto.10 Ora, fu osservato che alcune andavano colla testa troppo chinata verso terra e col collo storto, e colla vita piegata a destra a sinistra, dandosi nell'andare l'una all'altra urtoni e andando troppo distanti l'una dall'altra. E queste mancano di disinvoltura; altre poi andarono all'estremo opposto, voglio dire che levavano gli occhi alle finestre si portavano nelle botteghe a destra e a sinistra, li gettavano

dentro delle carrozze. E questo è difetto di sfacciataggine mondana, contraria alla modestia che deve avere una Figlia di Sant'Anna. Vi furono di quelle che per istrada parlavano, gestivano e ridevano; cosa contraria assai assai a quell'assoluto silenzio che vuole la Regola per le strade dentro delle Città o dei Paesi.

13. Così in qualcuna si dovette deplorare il difetto di separarsi alla casa dell'infermo dalla compagna uscendo fuori della camera sola per parlare con quei di casa; " questi sono difetti così rovinosi per l'Istituto che ad ogni modo quelle che vi hanno mancato [devono ad ogni modo emendarsene].

14. In alcune vi fu il difetto di pigrizia alla mattina, non essendo pronte a levarsi alle cinque al suono della campana; oppure per qualche poco di male, o di testa o di stomaco o d'altro male che sia, non andarono alla meditazione o vi andarono tardi, e ciò fecero senza averne la licenza della Superiora; così altre non furono pronte ad intervenire a tutti gli atti di comunità e alle preghiere ed a colazione, pranzo, cena ed alle ricreazioni.12

15. Ecco, sorelle, il motivo di dolore e di piangere che hanno alcune di voi: Ecco, sorelle, da quali difetti nell'anno incominciato del 77 deve mondarsi l'Istituto in alcune che ne fanno parte, questa emenda la domanda il Signore in riconoscenza di averci aspettate a misericordia, fino a questo nuovo anno; la domanda la Santa Madre che ci tiene nella sua famiglia, la domandano i nostri prossimi, i quali nulla di bene possono sperare dalle Sorelle rilassate anzi da esse saranno solo male edificati, e finalmente se non ci emendiamo non conseguiremo di essere ammesse a parte della gloria che gode la Santa Madre e con Essa godono quelle Sorelle che vissero quaggiù piene dello spirito di loro vocazione. Che il nostro Dio ci accordi tutte queste grazie come di cuore ne lo preghiamo.
